documents.unit: Digital Education / Hub for Teaching and Learning Resources
documents.title: Generative AI and Academic Integrity
documents.summary: The university page invites instructors to use AI but leaves the choice to each instructor, and tells students to check the professor, syllabus and assignment. Misuse falls under the Academic Code of Conduct, with informal and formal violations and sanctions, and AI detectors are not used in discipline.
documents.stance_why: The page says the choice 'rests solely on each individual instructor' and tells students to 'check with your professor, check your syllabus, and check per assignment'; it sets no university-wide rule and defers to instructors, so delegates. It adds ACC consequences and bars AI detectors.

units.why: The university 'invite[s]' instructors to 'integrate AI into their coursework wherever it is relevant and beneficial', a welcoming default toward AI addressed to instructors at course design; P02 fits because the stance is encouragement, while who decides is coded separately as P04.
units.anchor: invite our instructors to integrate AI into their coursework wherever it is relevant and beneficial
units.resolution_why: Both coded P02 for instructors at course design; A modality should, B may. 'We invite our instructors to integrate AI ... wherever it is relevant and beneficial' is a recommendation, not a bare permission, so should.

units.why: The decision to adopt AI 'rests solely on each individual instructor', so the university sets no rule itself and delegates per course and assignment; P04 fits because the point is who decides, not the default.
units.anchor: rests solely on each individual instructor
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, modality informs, neutral; B coded actor instructor, modality may, unit_stance permit. The source says the decision 'rests solely on each individual instructor': it states who decides and grants no permission itself, so it informs, neutral, addressed to all readers. Type P04 agreed.

units.why: The page says U-M 'has devised robust, private AI tools exclusively for our faculty, staff, and students'; these are institution-wide tools rather than one course's tool, so P92 rather than P17.
units.anchor: U-M has devised robust, private AI tools exclusively for our faculty, staff, and students
units.policy: U-M has devised robust, private AI tools exclusively for its faculty, staff, and students.
units.fit_note: States that the tools exist; it does not tell anyone to use them.

units.why: Students are told to 'refer to the course syllabus or consult their respective instructors' on permissible AI uses; this places the duty to learn each course's rules on students, so P78 (find out and follow the rules), with the ask-the-instructor element secondary.
units.anchor: refer to the course syllabus or consult their respective instructors for clarifications
units.policy: Students are recommended to refer to the course syllabus or consult their instructors for clarifications on the permissible uses of AI within each course.
units.fit_note: Also says to consult the instructor (P10), but as a first step, not only when unsure.

units.why: Unethical use or use 'against instructor directions' is 'a direct violation of the UM-Dearborn Academic Code of Conduct', which classes misuse as misconduct under an integrity code (P36).
units.anchor: AI tools are used unethically or against instructor directions, it would be a direct violation
units.policy: If AI tools are used unethically or against instructor directions, it is a direct violation of the UM-Dearborn Academic Code of Conduct (ACC).
units.resolution_why: Both coded P36, student, when-misuse, prohibit; A must-not, B informs. The source says unethical use or use 'against instructor directions' 'would be a direct violation' of the ACC, which in effect forbids it, so must-not.

units.why: Students are told to 'check with your professor, check your syllabus, and check per assignment' before using AI on graded work; it makes students responsible for finding the applicable rule (P78) rather than only asking when unsure (P10).
units.anchor: check with your professor, check your syllabus, and check per assignment
units.fit_note: Includes checking with the professor (P10) and checking per assignment.
units.resolution_why: A coded P78, course-start, must; B coded P10, during-work, should. The source answers 'Can I use AI...' with 'check with your professor, check your syllabus, and check per assignment': a duty to find the rules (syllabus, professor, assignment) rather than only asking when unsure, so P78; phase course-start matches the other P78 unit. 'Ensures you approach each assignment ... with the utmost integrity' is advice, not a stated requirement, so should.

units.why: 'you will need to do this per individual course as professors have varying expectations' says one course's AI rule does not carry over to another, which is P11.
units.anchor: you will need to do this per individual course as professors have varying expectations

units.why: 'AI should be used as a collaborative tool, not as a sole source of academic creation' keeps the student as primary author and thinker, so P32 rather than P19 (which is about banning submitted AI output).
units.anchor: should be used as a collaborative tool, not as a sole source of academic creation

units.why: Once AI is permitted, it 'can increase learning by constructing study aids'; this is a permitted use of AI for study aids and review, so P14.
units.anchor: AI can increase learning by constructing study aids
units.policy: AI can increase learning by constructing study aids.
units.fit_note: Offered as an example of beneficial use, once the course permits AI.

units.why: The same sentence says AI can increase learning by 'brainstorming material', a permitted use matching P15.
units.anchor: brainstorming material
units.policy: AI can increase learning by brainstorming material.
units.fit_note: Offered as an example of beneficial use, once the course permits AI.

units.why: The same sentence names 'improving grammar' as a beneficial use; this is AI for editing and writing support, so P91 rather than P18.
units.anchor: improving grammar
units.policy: AI can increase learning by improving grammar.
units.fit_note: Offered as an example of beneficial use, once the course permits AI.

units.why: Students 'should NOT use AI as a sole author for original works/assignments ... without the explicit approval of your instructor'; P19 fits because the AI may not produce the submitted work, but the rule is limited to sole authorship and has an instructor-approval exception.
units.anchor: should NOT use AI as a sole author for original works/assignments
units.policy: Students should not use AI as a sole author for original works or assignments (writings, art, presentations, etc.) without the explicit approval of their instructor.
units.fit_note: Bans only sole authorship and allows it with explicit instructor approval (P107).
units.resolution_why: A normalized the policy, B left it null; both P19. The anchor omits the 'without the explicit approval of your instructor' exception, so the normalized statement, faithful to the full sentence, is kept.

units.why: 'If you use AI in a course in which it is prohibited, you may be found responsible for violating the ACC' ties prohibited use to the integrity code; P36 fits because misuse is handled as an ACC violation.
units.anchor: you may be found responsible for violating the ACC
units.resolution_why: Both coded P36, student, when-misuse, informs; unit_stance A neutral, B prohibit. The sentence reports a consequence of using AI where it is prohibited and sets no new prohibition, so neutral.

units.why: 'Each student is allotted two informal violations in their academic career' states a concrete consequence structure in advance, so P37; it is not a penalty list, hence the fit note.
units.anchor: Each student is allotted two informal violations in their academic career
units.fit_note: Describes a limit on informal violations rather than a penalty itself.

units.why: States that informal violations are 'not stored in the university’s database', a record consequence announced in advance (P37).
units.anchor: Informal violations are not stored in the university’s database
units.fit_note: Describes record-keeping rather than a penalty.

units.why: 'Formal violations are stored in the university database and are visible on a student’s academic record' is a stated consequence announced in advance; P37.
units.anchor: Formal violations are stored in the university database
units.fit_note: Describes record-keeping and visibility timing rather than a penalty.

units.why: 'Students with formal violations or ineligible for the following for one year' (Chancellor's Medallion, Dean's List, honor scholar, paid tutoring or grading positions, college scholarships) states concrete consequences in advance, so P37.
units.anchor: Students with formal violations or ineligible for the following for one year
units.fit_note: Lists loss of honors, positions and scholarships, not grade penalties.
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance restrict, B neutral. The list of lost honors and positions is a consequence, not a position on AI use, so neutral.

units.why: Lists 'Reduced or failing grade on an assignment' as a possible academic sanction, a concrete penalty stated in advance (P37).
units.anchor: Reduced or failing grade on an assignment
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this as its own unit; B merged both grade sanctions into one unit anchored on the course sentence. The source lists two sanctions on separate lines ('Reduced or failing grade on an assignment' and 'for the course'), so both are kept, P37.

units.why: Lists 'Reduced or failing grade for the course' as a possible academic sanction, a concrete penalty stated in advance (P37).
units.anchor: Reduced or failing grade for the course

units.why: Says detectors 'have been found to falsely indicate that human-written text was created by GenAI', giving the reliability reason for not relying on them (P39).
units.anchor: AI Detection systems have been found to falsely indicate that human-written text
units.resolution_why: Both coded P39, informs; phase A when-misuse, B general. The sentence gives the reliability reason for detectors in the discipline section, so when-misuse.

units.why: Says that with AI detection 'there is no original source/origin or tangible evidence available', a point about what counts as evidence; P69 (evidence standards) rather than P39 because it addresses evidence, not reliability.
units.anchor: there is no original source/origin or tangible evidence available with AI Detection
units.fit_note: Contrasts AI detection with plagiarism checkers on evidence; also touches evidence standards (P69) but sets no explicit standard.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this separately (P69); B folded it into the reliability unit. The source says detectors give 'no original source/origin or tangible evidence'; this is a rationale for not relying on detectors, not an evidence standard for misuse findings, so P39 rather than P69, with the P69 aspect noted.

units.why: 'UM-Dearborn will not be adopting an official AI Detection system' states the institution will not use detectors, matching P39.
units.anchor: UM-Dearborn will not be adopting an official AI Detection system
units.resolution_why: Both coded P39, admin, when-misuse; A must-not, B informs. 'will not be adopting an official AI Detection system' is an institutional commitment, so must-not.

units.why: 'results from third-party AI Detection systems ... cannot be used in disciplinary actions (informal or formal)' bars detector output as evidence entirely; P39 (not relied on as proof) fits better than P69 because detector results are excluded outright, not weighed.
units.anchor: cannot be used in disciplinary actions (informal or formal) with students
units.fit_note: Also a rule on what evidence may be used in discipline (P69).
units.resolution_why: A and B agree on P39, instructor, when-misuse, must-not. A noted the evidence-standard aspect (P69) in fit_note; kept, since the passage bars detector results outright rather than weighing them.

documents.unit: Digital Education / Hub for Teaching and Learning Resources
documents.title: Generative AI for Faculty
documents.summary: A Hub page for faculty suggesting how to teach with AI: set class norms, share prompts, evaluate AI output. It weighs benefits against ethical and privacy concerns, describes the privacy-protecting free U-M GPT, and lists Hub consultations.
documents.stance_why: The page gives considerations ('Establish class norms', 'Design assignments where students are invited to use generative AI') and Hub consultation offers but sets no rule for students; the choice stays with instructors, so delegates.

units.why: Instructors are told to 'Establish class norms for appropriate use of Generative AI', which is stating expectations to students, so P09 is nearest.
units.anchor: Establish class norms for appropriate use of Generative AI
units.fit_note: Asks for class norms generally, not specifically a syllabus statement (P09 considered).
units.resolution_why: A coded P09 and split off the 'Being up front' sentence as P66; B coded one P66 unit. The source asks for class norms generally and does not ask for a syllabus statement, so P09 does not fit; P66 (explain and discuss rules with students) does. unit_stance neutral (B) since it takes no position on AI.

units.why: 'Being up front with students can encourage them to be more respectful in their use of these tools' explains why to state norms openly and discuss with students; P66.
units.anchor: Being up front with students can encourage them to be more respectful in their use
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this sentence separately (B included it in its P66 unit). It is the stated reason for setting norms, so it is kept, P66.

units.why: Instructors should 'Design assignments where students are invited to use generative AI', redesigning assignments around AI (P35) rather than only permitting it.
units.anchor: Design assignments where students are invited to use generative AI

units.why: The rationale that inviting AI use 'helps students learn appropriate ways to use these technologies so they can be more successful' is about teaching effective AI use (P44).
units.anchor: helps students learn appropriate ways to use these technologies so they can be
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this rationale as a unit (P44); B left it inside the P35 unit. The source says inviting AI use helps students learn appropriate use 'so they can be more successful'; a real statement about teaching AI use, so kept.

units.why: Instructors should 'Require students to share sequence of prompts and output generated', a transcript/log requirement (P26).
units.anchor: Require students to share sequence of prompts and output generated
units.resolution_why: Both coded P26, instructor, should, require; phase A before-course, B during-work. This is an instructor assignment-design step like the P35 and P31 units on the same page, so before-course.

units.why: Says shared prompts 'can help you learn more about what students understand as well as the misconceptions they may have', using the transcripts to check understanding; P34 is nearest.
units.anchor: learn more about what students understand as well as the misconceptions they may have
units.fit_note: Checks understanding through prompt logs rather than reviews, interviews or oral exams.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this (P34); B included it in the P26 unit. It says shared prompts let the instructor see what students understand, a check on understanding but not by review or oral exam, so kept with the fit note.

units.why: Instructors should 'Have students analyze, evaluate, and revise generated content for ... accuracy, bias, and hallucinations', building verification of AI output into assignments (P31).
units.anchor: students analyze, evaluate, and revise generated content for things such as accuracy, bias
units.fit_note: Framed as an instructor assignment design, not a student duty.
units.resolution_why: Both coded P31, instructor, should; phase A before-course, B during-work; unit_stance A encourage, B require. The source says 'Have students analyze, evaluate, and revise ...' as a design suggestion in a list of considerations, so before-course and encourage.

units.why: 'reinforcing the need to fact check the content that is generated' states that students must verify AI output, so P31.
units.anchor: reinforcing the need to fact check the content that is generated
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this as a separate student-facing point (P31); B folded it into one unit. The source says the exercise reinforces 'the need to fact check', so kept.

units.why: Names benefits ('Speeding up content creation, idea generation, and editing') for teaching and learning without a rule; P87.
units.anchor: Speeding up content creation, idea generation, and editing are real

units.why: Lists 'ethical considerations, privacy concerns, the potential for bias in AI algorithms' as real challenges; P53 (bias and harms).
units.anchor: questions about ethical considerations, privacy concerns, the potential for bias in AI algorithms

units.why: 'it is essential to weigh its potential against these challenges' asks users to balance gains and risks before using AI; P118.
units.anchor: it is essential to weigh its potential against these challenges
units.resolution_why: Both coded P118, instructor, should; phase A before-course, B general. It is a general principle about weighing potential against challenges, so general.

units.why: 'prompts and outputs are not shared with OpenAI or any other provider' states a privacy benefit of the university tool, matching P50 (prefer vetted tools, protect data).
units.anchor: prompts and outputs are not shared with OpenAI or any other provider

units.why: Describes 'U-M GPT' as a 'university maintained portal to several Large Language Models'; an institution-wide provided tool, so P92 rather than P17.
units.anchor: U-M GPT is university maintained portal to several Large Language Models

units.why: 'There is no charge for U-M GPT' is an access and cost fact, matching P51.
units.anchor: There is no charge for U-M GPT
units.fit_note: Notes free access but also that other supported tools cost money; it does not require free alternatives.

units.why: 'Anyone with a university login can access U-M GPT' says the provided tool is open to the community; P92.
units.anchor: Anyone with a university login can access U-M GPT
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this (P92); B mentioned it inside its P92 rationale. A separate sentence on who can access the tool, so kept.

units.why: 'You should expect to revise prompts to get better outputs' is practical prompting advice (P93).
units.anchor: You should expect to revise prompts to get better outputs
units.resolution_why: Both coded P93, all, should; phase A during-work, B general. Revising prompts happens while working with the tool, so during-work.

units.why: Says AI tools 'can be useful in generating ideas for assignments, rubrics, discussion prompts, presentations, quiz/test questions' meaning instructors' own teaching work (P59).
units.anchor: useful in generating ideas for assignments, rubrics, discussion prompts, presentations, quiz/test questions

units.why: Points instructors to an outside 'AI resource site for professors and instructors' as a source of further tools, directing readers to more guidance (P115).
units.anchor: check out Old Dominion's AI resource site for professors and instructors
units.resolution_why: Both coded P115, instructor, may; phase A before-course, B general. It points to outside resources with no tie to a course stage, so general.

units.why: The Hub offers to 'Schedule a one-on-one GenAI consultation with an Instructional Designer', support for faculty learning about AI (P63).
units.anchor: Schedule a one-on-one GenAI consultation with an Instructional Designer

units.why: The Hub offers help to 'Develop a class policy around GenAI (we have a GenAI tool that can help)', faculty support for setting course policy; P63 rather than P110 because no template is shown.
units.anchor: Develop a class policy around GenAI (we have a GenAI tool that can help)
units.fit_note: Help is with writing the course policy, with a tool, not supplied sample syllabus language; not only learning about AI (P63 considered).
units.resolution_why: A coded P63, B coded P110 with a fit note. The Hub offers a GenAI tool that helps draft a class policy, closer to providing policy templates than to helping faculty learn AI, so P110 with a fit note.

units.why: The Hub offers to 'Stress test an assignment', helping instructors check assignments against AI; P63.
units.anchor: Stress test an assignment
units.fit_note: Also about assignment redesign (P35).
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this list item separately (B grouped it with the consultation); a real offer of faculty support, P63.

units.why: The Hub offers help to 'Design an assignment that uses GenAI', support for faculty planning AI-based work; P63.
units.anchor: Design an assignment that uses GenAI
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this list item separately (B grouped it); a real offer of faculty support, P63.

units.why: Calls the Hub guide a 'living document' and says it is 'Always being updated', so the guidance is provisional (P54).
units.anchor: This is a living document of some length

units.why: Offers a 'Video Presentation Getting Started with AI Literacy', AI-literacy training for the community (P70).
units.anchor: Getting Started with AI Literacy

units.why: The Hub discloses that its welcome text 'was generated by ChatGPT 4.0', an example of disclosing its own AI use; P47 is nearest although the audience is faculty readers of the site.
units.anchor: That text was generated by ChatGPT 4.0 when prompted to generate a welcome message
units.fit_note: Disclosure by the Hub on its website, not by an instructor to students.
units.resolution_why: Only A coded this (P47). The Hub says its welcome text 'was generated by ChatGPT 4.0', an example of disclosing AI use that faculty readers see modeled; kept with A's fit note because it explains an AI-use practice, though it is not a rule.

notes: Course layer deferred in the collect file; no school or computing policy found. Page text came from a browser re-collection. P37 was used for several record-keeping consequences (fit notes), and the final P39 vs P69 choice for third-party detector results is flagged in a fit note. Reconciled by comparing coder A and coder B against the saved page texts. B's free-form topic labels were replaced by A's codebook topics. The Hub's AI-generated welcome text unit (P47) was kept, with A's fit note, though it is a modeled practice rather than a rule.
